The generic adopt-axis path makes win-rate, cost/token, and adoption claims without structured provenance.
Axis processing is linear over aggregates with one bounded candidate sort; no per-request nested scan or new unprobed surface was found.
Tests cover hostile-label newline/backtick sanitization and scoped marker matching; no production write, egress, or executable user input occurs.
Tests exercise thresholds, exact-label provenance, cost coverage, proof tier, stale/undated/future evidence, truncation caveats, and illustrative-fix validity.
This is unit-test code and is not on an ingest, request, render, or bundle hot path.
Ledger labels are length-limited, single-lined, and backtick-stripped before prose/snippet use; raw labels remain structured provenance only, with no execution or write path.

Per-variation thresholds, arithmetic, paired-cost coverage, structured field provenance, observational proof tier, truncation, and stale/undatable demotion were checked and are internally reproducible.
The detector performs linear filtering plus a single sort over the bounded variation aggregate and does not repeatedly recompute source data.
Command fixtures remain inert strings, and tests cover parser fail-closed behavior for conditional, unreachable, malformed, quoted, and path-restore commands.
Tests reproduce S1/S2 signatures, transcript ordering, failed-command exclusion, false-positive controls, severity arithmetic, provenance field, and as-of date.
This is unit-test code and does not run in the production detector hot path.

The detector bounds its inference to attempted command signatures, cites the precise parsed-command field, reports affected-session counts, supplies an as-of date, and avoids claiming proven Git effects.
Each session's calls and projected command segments are scanned linearly; evidence is capped at five rows and no N× recomputation was found.
The test only constructs inert tool-call and settings fixtures; it does not exercise an external command or client/server security boundary.
The fixture reproduces the 2-of-10 rollback threshold and verifies suppression when the recommended pre-edit hook already exists.
This is a small unit test outside production request and ingest paths.

Only allowlisted AXIS_COVERAGE keys reach the validated gh command snippet, so ledger-controlled arbitrary axes cannot inject shell syntax; the repository and labels are static.
Win, cost/token, and catalog-coverage claims are emitted without structured provenance or an as-of/staleness signal.
The detector performs one filter, one sort, and bounded aggregate mapping over axis summaries; no ingest-memory or request-latency hotspot was found.
The test verifies deletion commands quote each absolute path and include the -- option terminator; commands remain inert assertions and are not executed.

findings.title: Generic shadow-axis adoption claims omit structured provenance
findings.what: The generic adopt-axis recommendation derives win rate, evidence mix, average cost/token delta, and an adoption action at lines 122-140, but returns only display-oriented evidence strings. It supplies no RecProvenance observations identifying the aggregate artifact and fields, so the recommendation's claims are not reproducible through the structured provenance contract. The separate recs-axis path does provide provenance, confirming this omission is path-specific.
findings.fix: Add provenance to adoptAxisRec with observations for byAxis axis/sample/win counts, live/replay counts, and the paired cost or token sums/counts used by the averages; state the threshold/adoption inference and include a trustworthy asOf or explicitly demote undated evidence.
findings.acceptance: A qualifying non-recs axis recommendation passes validateRecommendationProvenance, names the exact parse-shadow-calls aggregate fields behind every numeric claim, and tests demonstrate stale or undated inputs cannot read as a current standing default.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read of lines 118-143 confirmed the generic return ends after evidence and fix with no provenance. Lines 177-199 and 230-253 in the same dispatched file provide structured provenance only for the separate recsFindingVerdict path, so they do not cure the generic path.

findings.title: Undo-rate recommendation is not reproducible or dated
findings.what: The detector claims a precise rollback percentage, invocation count, affected count, and '2+ wasted round-trips' at lines 47-51, but emits neither structured provenance nor an as-of date. Consumers therefore cannot trace the calculation to computeToolEffectiveness fields or tell whether the historical signal is current.
findings.fix: Attach RecProvenance observations citing the tool-effectiveness artifact and tool/invocations/immediatelyFollowedByUndo fields, document the division and rounding inference, source an ISO asOf date from the contributing observation window, and demote stale evidence to explicit 'as of <date>' wording.
findings.acceptance: The 2-of-10 fixture produces 20% with provenance that cites both operands and the source artifact; provenance validation passes, and a stale-window fixture renders an explicit as-of date instead of an unqualified present-tense claim.
findings.verifyNote: A focused second pass over lines 42-75 confirmed the returned object has evidence and an illustrative fix but no provenance. The arithmetic itself re-derives correctly as immediatelyFollowedByUndo / invocations, so the finding is limited to reproducibility and historical dating.

findings.title: Uncovered-axis discovery claims lack provenance and freshness
findings.what: The recommendation asserts a shadow win ratio, experiment count, average cost/token advantage, and absence of a covering detector at lines 93-106, then offers a validated issue-filing command, but supplies no structured provenance. It also has no timestamp or stale/undated caveat, so historical ledger evidence is presented as a current discovery.
findings.fix: Add observations citing the selected byAxis entry and the exact win/sample/live/replay and cost-or-token sum/count fields, record the AXIS_COVERAGE lookup used for the catalog-gap claim, add the inference and asOf/stale state, and suppress or demote the issue-filing fix when evidence cannot be dated or is stale.
findings.acceptance: A qualifying uncovered axis passes provenance validation with reproducible operands for the percentage and average, identifies the coverage lookup, and stale or undated fixtures emit an explicit dated lead without a validated filing command.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read of lines 82-119 confirmed the recommendation ends with evidence and fix but no provenance or date. The axis is constrained by AXIS_COVERAGE before reaching the command, so shell injection was rejected as a candidate; the surviving defect is solely claim provenance and freshness.
